title: Rav Tavut
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites Bava Batra 49a: “Rav Pappi said: Ravina told me: A certain scholar told me — and Rav Tavut is his name — who, if they gave him all the wealth in the world, would not alter his words: ‘A case happened to me. On the eve of Shabbat a man came and asked me whether I had sesame to sell. I told him no. He said to me, “Let these zuz be deposited with you, for it is getting dark for me.” I said to him, “Here is the house before you” … and they were stolen. He came before Rava,’” etc. In [Chullin 44a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.44a.6) he resolves Rava’s words. Likewise there, at [49b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.49b.14), he refers to Rava’s words and says: “The power of the son (Rav Huna son of Rav Nachman) is greater than the power of the father (Rav Nachman).”[^1]

notes.text: The sesame story begins at [Bava Metzia 49a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.49a.16) and continues at [49b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.49b.1) through the deposit, the theft and the appearance before Rava. The consulted text gives Rav Shmuel bar Zutra as an alternative name. Compare [Heilprin’s notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1577&lang=en).
